sources.citation: Shintani, Tadahiko L. A. 2025. Kayan-kei gengo no bunrui [Classification of Kayan languages]. In Sawada Hideo (ed.), Toward construction of a typological and genetic overview of minority languages in Burma, 135-146. Tokyo: ILCAA. doi 10.15026/0002001132
sources.note: Japanese; says the former 'Pado-Thaido-Gekho' group (2003 classification) has since been surveyed and published in the LSTCA series; tone system only; no stress; reference list gives LSTCA 106 Kadaw, 116 Thaidai (not 111 Gokhu).

sources.citation: Kato, Atsuhiko. 2021. Typological profile of Karenic languages. In P. Sidwell & M. Jenny (eds.), The Languages and Linguistics of Mainland Southeast Asia, ch. 18. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Family-level only: after describing Eastern Pwo sesquisyllables as 'composed of the unstressed first syllable and the stressed second syllable', says 'Karenic languages generally have sesquisyllabic words' (with Kayah Li and Kayan examples from Solnit 1997 and Manson 2010). Gek(h)o appears only in the ethnic-group list and in a negation-typology list; no Geko-specific statement.
